source_text: hm... I am not sure what the standard practice is for XTDB, but I think insertion time vs record time can differ without any issue

fragments.text: I am not sure what the standard practice is for XTDB, but I think insertion time vs record time can differ without any issue

reply_text:
You're right, and it means futon1b doesn't need changing. I'm testing the route it already has on the scratch server:㊥ ("can differ without any issue") Agreed, so futon1b doesn't need changing. XTDB keeps two separate clocks. System time records when minus40 imported a row, and there's no reason to fake it. Valid time records when a memory version actually held, and we can set that to any date.

㊬ (checked just now) futon1b's existing hyperedge route already takes `:hx/valid-time`. On the scratch store I wrote two versions of one hyperedge, valid from 09-01 and 09-20. Querying at 08-15 returned nothing, at 09-10 returned v1, and at 10-01 returned v2.

㊭ (milestone 2 plan)
- Each memory gets one stable `:memory/version` hyperedge.
- That hyperedge is written once per version found in the transcripts' edit history. Its valid time is the edit time, and it points at that version's evidence entry.
- "What did this memory say on date X" then becomes a single valid-time query.

㊟ (one constraint) Versions have to be replayed oldest first. A write with no end date stays valid indefinitely, so writing an older version after a newer one would overwrite the newer one.

㊢ (recorded) I've updated the plan in the README (`a80af71`) and in my memory note. Shall I start on the transcript replay?
